author: Josh Wingrove
description: President Donald Trump’s fixation on Greenland offers an ice-cold reminder to leaders in Europe and abroad: No deal is ever final.
title: Trump’s Greenland Pressure Blitz Reopens Tariff Wounds in Europe

author: Josh Wingrove, Saleha Mohsin, Joshua Green
description: The candidacy of BlackRock’s Rick Rieder to be the next Federal Reserve chair has gained late momentum, people familiar with the matter say, as President Donald Trump weighs congressional blowback in his bid to put a friendlier face at the head of the central bank.
title: BlackRock’s Rick Rieder Bid for Fed Chair Is Gaining Traction

author: Maria Paula Mijares Torres
description: Democrat Abigail Spanberger was sworn in as governor of the Commonwealth of Virginia on Saturday, becoming the state’s first female leader.
title: Democrat Spanberger Sworn in as Virginia’s First Female Governor

author: Alberto Nardelli, Alex Wickham
description: The Trump administration is asking countries that want a permanent spot on his new Board of Peace to contribute at least $1 billion.
title: Trump Wants Nations to Pay $1 Billion to Stay on His Peace Board

author: Tony Czuczka
description: A US strike in Syria killed an “experienced terrorist leader” with links to an Islamic State attacker who killed three Americans in an ambush in the city of Palmyra in December, US Central Command said in a statement.
title: US Says Strike in Syria Killed Plotter of Islamic State Attacks

author: Alicia A. Caldwell, Maria Paula Mijares Torres
description: Anti-ICE protesters in Minneapolis overwhelmed a planned rally in support of Immigration and Customs Enforcement on Saturday, pelting the supporters with snowballs and water balloons in sub-freezing weather.
title: Anti-ICE Demonstrators Outnumber Backers in Minneapolis Protest

description: Pardoned January 6th rioter and GOP Florida Senate candidate Jake Lang pulled into crowd of protestors in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Jake Lang Pulled Into Crowd of Protestors in Minneapolis

author: Richard Bravo
description: European Union lawmakers are poised to halt approval of the EU’s trade deal with the US over President Donald Trump’s vow to impose tariffs on countries that supported Greenland in the face of American threats.
title: EU Set to Halt US Trade Deal Over Trump’s New Tariff Threat

description: Virginia's first female democratic governor Abigail Spanberger sworn in at the state capitol in Richmond, Virginia. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Virginia's First Female Governor Sworn Into Office

author: Josh Wingrove, Maria Paula Mijares Torres
description: President Donald Trump railed against JPMorgan Chase & Co. and its leader Jamie Dimon, threatening to sue the banking giant over his claim that he was debanked after the Jan. 6, 2021, Capitol riot.
title: Trump Blasts Dimon, Threatens to Sue JPMorgan Over Debanking

author: Thomas Seal, Laura Dhillon Kane, Danielle Bochove
description: Canada has long stuck closely to the US on China policy, even through a diplomatic crisis over high-profile prisoners. Along with historic trade ties, that alignment is now cracking.
title: Carney’s China Embrace Widens Gap With US in Trump’s Tariff Era

author: Mohamed Omar Ahmed
description: Somalia’s President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud said Israel’s decision to recognize Somaliland has been rejected globally and domestically, adding that Somalia’s unity is “non-negotiable.”
title: Somalia’s President Condemns Israel’s Recognition of Somaliland

author: Daniel Carvalho, Beatriz Reis
description: The European Union and Mercosur officially signed one of the world’s largest free trade agreements on Saturday, clinching a deal that has been in the works for more than two decades.
title: EU Inks South America Trade Deal After 25 Years of Negotiations

author: Mihir Mishra
description: India’s Directorate General of Civil Aviation said late Saturday that it imposed a penalty of over 220 million rupees ($2.4 million) on IndiGo and chided the airline’s executives over their December flight cancellations.
title: India Regulator Fines IndiGo $2.4 Million Over December Meltdown

author: Sam Kim (News)
description: President Trump says he’ll be “suing JPMorgan Chase over the next two weeks for incorrectly and inappropriately DEBANKING me” after the January 6 protests.
title: Trump Says He’ll Sue JPMorgan in Coming Weeks for ‘Debanking Me’

author: Josh Wingrove, Maria Paula Mijares Torres
description: President Donald Trump announced a 10% tariff on goods from European countries rallying to Denmark’s side in his pursuit of Greenland, a dramatic escalation in the standoff that will further strain US ties with many of its closest allies.
title: Trump to Impose Tariffs on 8 European Nations Over Greenland

author: Ougna Camara
description: Guinea’s former military leader Mamadi Doumbouya has been sworn in as president for a seven-year term, marking a return to constitutional order in the West African nation four years after a putsch.
title: Guinea Former Military Leader Doumbouya Sworn In as President

author: Kok Leong Chan, Netty Idayu Ismail
description: The United Malays National Organization, a key member of Malaysia’s ruling coalition, is cooperating with the nation’s Malay-Muslim opposition parties, hinting at the possibility of a shift in alliances after the next general election.
title: Malaysia’s Once-Dominant UMNO to Work With Political Rivals

author: Anthony Capaccio
description: The Army has once again missed its own deadline for fielding the first US hypersonic weapon, in a sign that one of the Pentagon’s top priorities is still behind schedule.
title: Army Hypersonic Missile Fielding Falters on Missed Deadline

author: Kamailoudini Tagba
description: Ivory Coast lawmakers elected a former prime minister from Alassane Ouattara’s ruling party as speaker of parliament, nearly a month after legislative elections held in late December.
title: Ivory Coast Lawmakers Name Ex-PM Achi as Parliament Speaker

author: Ros Krasny
description: Constant airstrikes by Kremlin forces are undermining “even the small opportunities for dialogue” between Kyiv and Moscow, said President Volodymyr Zelenskiy.
title: Zelenskiy Says Russian Strikes Undermine Prospects for Dialogue

author: Crayton Harrison
description: María Corina Machado’s charm offensive in the Trump White House, complete with a shiny Nobel medal in an elegant frame, is part of a recalibrated effort by the leader of Venezuela’s opposition to reclaim the narrative about the country’s transformation.
title: Machado Takes a New Tack to Win Trump’s Backing on Venezuela

author: Fred Ojambo
description: Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni was declared the winner of elections that the main opposition said were marred by rigging from the outset, extending his four-decade rule.
title: Museveni Declared Winner of Uganda Vote as Opposition Cries Foul

author: Sara Sjolin
description: Thousands of people took to the streets across Denmark to protest US President Donald Trump’s ambitions to take control of Greenland, underscoring the deep unease over the future of the Arctic island.
title: Trump’s Greenland Demands Spark Protest Rallies Across Denmark

author: Dan Williams
description: Argentina’s Javier Milei and Turkey’s Recep Tayyip Erdogan are among world leaders who have been invited to join Donald Trump’s so-called Board of Peace, as the US pushes ahead with its peace plan for the Palestinian enclave of Gaza.
title: Milei, Erdogan Invited to Join Trump’s Gaza ‘Board of Peace’

author: Eric Ombok
description: The US escalated its criticism of South Africa after naval exercises this week involving China and some of the BRICS member nations.
title: US Ratchets Up Criticism of South Africa After BRICS War Games

author: Arsalan Shahla
description: Iran’s Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei on Saturday said “several thousand people” died in this month’s anti-government demonstrations, his first acknowledgment of the deadly scale of the unrest.
title: Iran’s Supreme Leader Acknowledges Thousands Killed In Unrest

author: Ewa Krukowska, John Ainger
description: The European Union is set to propose a swathe of new conditions to ensure local companies are prioritized when investment decisions are made in the region by member-states and foreign firms, upending a free-trade philosophy that has governed decades of policy.
title: EU Aims to Fight Industrial Decline With ‘Made in Europe’ Law

author: Volodymyr Verbianyi
description: In the wake of a damaging corruption scandal, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy is increasingly reaching out to potential political rivals as the prospect of an election becomes more likely.
title: Zelenskiy Courts Potential Challengers With US Calling for Vote

author: Ying Tian
description: China has issued a draft law to strengthen its national reserve system, manage major risks and modernize reserve governance, the National Development and Reform Commission said in a Saturday statement.
title: China Drafts Law to Safeguard Security of National Reserves

author: Kamil Kowalcze, Samy Adghirni, Daniel Hornak
description: Europe’s far-right parties are reassessing their ties to President Donald Trump after he used military force to oust Venezuela’s leader, Nicolás Maduro, and threatened to annex Greenland.
title: Trump’s Greenland Play Is a Step Too Far for Europe’s Far Right

author: Lucy White
description: Reform UK’s embrace of the most popular member of the Conservative shadow cabinet this week risks stoking internal strife within Nigel Farage’s populist party.
title: Farage Allies Foresee Tension in Jenrick’s Defection to Reform

author: Fred Ojambo
description: Uganda’s main opposition leader Bobi Wine, who’s vying for a second time to unseat President Yoweri Museveni, was taken away from his home late Friday.
title: Ugandan Opposition Says Party Leader Bobi Wine Abducted

author: Sharon Klyne
description: Australia is dropping a proposal to broadly criminalize hate speech as part of its response to last month’s deadly shooting in Sydney, after facing objection from major opposition parties.
title: Australia Changes Tack on Hate Crime Bills as Opposition Demurs

author: Alex Wickham
description: When Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch accused her rival Robert Jenrick of treachery and sacked him this week, some in Keir Starmer’s Labour government wondered: if the UK prime minister were stronger, would he do the same with Wes Streeting?
title: How Streeting Became Starmer’s Top UK Rival in Year of Grudges

author: Patpicha Tanakasempipat
description: Thailand’s ruling party, which is seeking to retain power in next month’s election, is vowing to resolve the country’s conflict with Cambodia and clean up its image as a transit hub for trafficked scam victims.
title: Thai Ruling Party Vows to Resolve Cambodia Row as Election Nears

author: John Gittelsohn
description: Rick Caruso, a billionaire real estate developer, will not run for California governor or mayor of Los Angeles, he announced on X Friday.
title: LA Billionaire Caruso to Skip 2026 Races for LA Mayor and California Governor

author: Erik Larson
description: A judge restricted the use of force by ICE officers in Minneapolis after protesters complained of widespread abuse that violated their constitutional rights, in a suit that’s taken on fresh urgency after a federal agent shot and killed a woman in her car.
title: Minneapolis Protesters Win Ruling Curbing ICE Use of Force

description: "Balance of Power: Late Edition" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Rep. Katherine Clark (D-MA) states ICE is a reign of terror and needs accountability when discussing her hearing in Minnesota about people impacted by ICE raids. Michael Allen, Beacon Global Strategies Managing Director, discusses the latest Trump geopolitical news. Representative Mike Flood (R-NE) shares his thoughts on whether or not large companies should pay for surging power costs.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Moves to Tech Giants to Pay Surging Power Costs | Balance of Power: Late Edition 01/16/2026

author: Toru Fujioka
description: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi will consider a temporary suspension of sales tax on food as part of her election campaign pledge after her expected dissolution of parliament next week, Mainichi newspaper reported, citing unnamed people familiar with the matter.
title: Takaichi to Mull Suspension of Food Sales Tax, Mainichi Reports
